mainTopic: Which כתובה payments are valid: the minor husband or convert, and the order of priority between two wives and their heirs.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier case. A woman holds both a גט and a כתובה from the same husband. If the גט is dated first, she collects two כתובות. If the כתובה is dated first, she collects only one. Next a משנה rules that the כתובה of a husband who married as a קטן, or of a גר who converted together with his wife, stays valid. רב הונא limits this to the basic מנה or מאתיים, while רב יהודה says she collects the תוספת too. A ברייתא refutes רב יהודה, and the גמרא explains that the משנה's words misled him. After the הדרן, a new chapter begins with a משנה on which of two wives, or their heirs, collects first from a dead husband's estate. The גמרא tries in two opposite versions to learn from the משנה's wording whether a later creditor who collected first keeps what he took. Each attempt is pushed back, and the second rejection finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the previous case: the order of the dates decides
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the earlier discussion: if the גט is dated before the כתובה, she collects two כתובות. If the כתובה is dated before the גט, she collects only one, because a man who remarries his ex-wife does so on the basis of the first כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the divorce document is dated earlier than the marriage contract, she collects two marriage contracts. If the marriage contract is dated earlier than the divorce document, she collects only one. That is because a man who divorces his wife and takes her back takes her back on the terms of the first marriage contract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the case from the previous page: a woman holds a גט and a כתובה from the same man. The order of their dates decides how much she can collect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט dated first shows she was divorced and then remarried. That makes the later כתובה a new contract for the second marriage, so she collects both. A כתובה dated first could simply be her original one, and we assume a man who remarries his ex-wife goes back to the first כתובה, so she collects only once.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract that guarantees the wife a payment if the marriage ends
On the condition / on the basis of

steps.whatToRemember: A גט dated before the כתובה means two כתובות. A כתובה dated before the גט means only one, because remarriage goes back to the first כתובה.

phrases.english: If the divorce document comes before the marriage contract,
phrases.notes: "Comes before" means its date is earlier.

phrases.english: she collects two marriage contracts.
If the marriage contract comes before the divorce document,
she collects only one marriage contract,
because one who divorces his wife and takes her back
took her back on the terms of the first marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion begun on the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The order of the dates decides: a גט dated first means two payments, a כתובה dated first means one.

steps.title: New משנה: the כתובה of a minor husband or a convert stays valid
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a father married off his son while the son was a קטן, or a גר converted together with his wife, her כתובה stays valid, because he kept her as his wife on those terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor whose father married him off: her marriage contract stays valid, because he kept her on that condition. A convert whose wife converted with him: her marriage contract stays valid, because he kept her on that condition.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a כתובה written when the husband had no legal power, as a קטן or as a non-Jew, still counts once he stays married to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband might argue that the old כתובה means nothing, because a קטן or a non-Jew cannot make a binding Jewish contract. The משנה answers that by staying married to her after he grew up or converted, he accepted those terms. So the כתובה is valid now.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, under the age of legal responsibility

phrases.english: MISHNAH: A minor whose father married him off:
her marriage contract stays valid,
phrases.notes: Even after he grows up, he can't say it doesn't count.

phrases.english: because it is on that condition that he kept her.
A convert whose wife converted along with him:
her marriage contract stays valid,
because it is on that condition that he kept her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתובה written by a קטן, or by a non-Jew before he converted with his wife, stays valid once he keeps her as his wife.

steps.title: רב הונא: only the basic amount, not the extra
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה: she collects only the basic מנה or מאתיים, but not the תוספת the husband added.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They taught this only about the basic one hundred or two hundred. But the extra amount, she does not get.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by narrowing the משנה. רב הונא says "her כתובה stays valid" covers only the standard minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic amount, a מנה or מאתיים, is set by the חכמים, so it does not depend on a valid contract. The תוספת is an extra promise the husband himself made. Since he made it as a קטן or a non-Jew, it does not bind him.

keyTerms.meaning: 100 or 200 זוז, the basic כתובה amounts
The extra amount the husband chose to add to the כתובה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the basic כתובה (a fixed amount set by the חכמים) with the תוספת (an extra amount the husband promised). This whole argument is only about the תוספת.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said:
They taught this only about the one hundred or two hundred,
phrases.notes: The basic amounts: 200 זוז for a woman who was a virgin at marriage, 100 for others.

phrases.english: but the extra amount, she does not get.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מָנֶה מָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far the משנה's ruling reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She collects only the basic מנה or מאתיים, not the תוספת.

steps.title: רב יהודה: she gets the extra amount too
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה disagrees with רב הונא and holds that she collects even the תוספת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: She gets even the extra amount.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives the opposite view. The whole כתובה stays valid, extra amount included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reads the משנה's reason, "on that condition he kept her," as covering everything written in the כתובה. By staying married to her, the husband took on the extra promise as well.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
She has even the extra amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תּוֹסֶפֶת יֵשׁ לָהּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She collects the תוספת as well as the basic amount.

steps.title: A ברייתא challenges רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: if they added an amount, she takes what they added. That suggests that if they did not add anything again, she gets no extra, which goes against רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: "If they added, she takes what they added." If they added, yes. If they did not add, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב יהודה. It reads it as saying she gets extra money only if the husband added it again after he grew up or converted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says she collects "what they added," meaning a new תוספת given later. The גמרא draws the opposite conclusion: without a new addition, the old תוספת written earlier does not count. That fits רב הונא and goes against רב יהודה.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If they added something new, she takes what they added.
phrases.notes: "They" means the husband, after he grew up or converted.

phrases.english: If they added, yes,
if they did not add, no!
phrases.notes: So the extra amount written in the old כתובה would not count, which is hard for רב יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's view using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that she collects the תוספת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets her collect only an amount added later. From this the גמרא infers that the original תוספת, written while he was a קטן or a non-Jew, is not collected.

steps.title: Maybe she collects the new amount on top of everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב יהודה by suggesting the ברייתא means she gets the added amount in addition to the full original כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it means: she even takes what they added.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof against רב יהודה. It offers another way to read the words 'she takes what they added.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier step read the ברייתא as 'she takes only what they added.' Here the גמרא suggests it means 'she also takes what they added,' on top of the whole first כתובה, including the תוספת. Read this way, the ברייתא no longer contradicts רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / you could read it as

phrases.english: Say: even what they added.
phrases.notes: He means she gets the new amount in addition to the whole original כתובה, not instead of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the inference drawn from the ברייתא in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference that she gets nothing beyond the new amount, not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's words can be read as adding to the old כתובה rather than replacing it

steps.title: The rest of the ברייתא rules out that reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the ending of the ברייתא makes clear that without a new addition she gets only the basic amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא does not teach that. It says: if they added something new, she takes what they added. If they did not add anything, a בתולה collects two hundred and an אלמנה collects one hundred!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense from step 6 by quoting the next words of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright that if nothing new was added, she gets only the basic מאתיים or מנה. So the original תוספת is lost, and the defense of רב יהודה fails.

keyTerms.meaning: But it does not teach this
a woman married for the first time as a virgin

phrases.english: But it does not teach this:
If they added something new, she takes what they added;
if they did not add, a virgin collects two hundred,
and a widow one hundred!
phrases.notes: She gets only the basic amount, with no extra from the original כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternate reading offered in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'even what they added' from step 6, and through it רב יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא states that without a new addition she gets only the basic amount. That reading leaves no room for her to keep the old תוספת.

steps.title: רב יהודה is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a final refutation of רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רב יהודה's position cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא is a final defeat. The halacha follows רב הונא: she collects the basic כתובה, but not the תוספת.
steps.whatToRemember: In these cases the כתובה stays valid only for the basic מנה or מאתיים, as רב הונא said. The תוספת is not collected unless it was added again.

phrases.english: A refutation of Rav Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final result of the challenge in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה is rejected. She collects only the basic כתובה, not the תוספת.

steps.title: How the משנה's wording misled רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב יהודה took 'her כתובה is valid' to mean the whole כתובה, when it really means only the basic amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה misled רב יהודה. He thought 'her כתובה remains valid' refers to the entire matter. But that is not so. It refers only to the main כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רב יהודה has been refuted, the גמרא explains where his mistake came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כתובתה קיימת' could seem to include everything written in the כתובה. The גמרא says they refer only to the basic amount set by חז"ל, the עיקר כתובה, and not to the extra the husband added.

keyTerms.meaning: her כתובה remains valid (the משנה's words)
the basic כתובה amount set by חז"ל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה itself was rejected. Only רב יהודה's understanding of its words was rejected.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, the mishna misled him;
he thought: "Her marriage contract remains valid" —
refers to the whole matter.
phrases.notes: He means the whole amount, including the extra the husband added.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
it refers to the main marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of the error after the refutation in step 8
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'כתובתה קיימת' in the משנה means only the עיקר כתובה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter הכותב לאשתו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the פרק הכותב לאשתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הכותב לאשתו.
steps.whatsHappening: This marks the end of the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional closing line said at the end of each פרק. It shows that the topic of this chapter is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: name of the chapter: 'One who writes to his wife'

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One who writes to his wife"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion

steps.title: With two wives, the first wife collects first
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that when a man who had two wives dies, the first wife's כתובה comes before the second's, and the same order applies to their heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man was married to two women and died, the first wife comes before the second. The heirs of the first wife come before the heirs of the second.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה about the order of collecting כתובות when there is not enough money for both wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first wife's כתובה was written earlier, so her claim on the estate comes first. The same order holds if both wives have died and their heirs come to collect.

keyTerms.meaning: one who was married (also the name of the new chapter)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the chapter's main theme: the order of priority when several claims are made on one estate.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים, וָמֵת —
phrases.english: One who was married to two women and died —
the first takes precedence over the second.
And the heirs of the first take precedence
over the heirs of the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה נָשׂוּי שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים, וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first wife collects her כתובה before the second, and her heirs come before the second wife's heirs.

steps.title: When the first wife died before her husband
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If the first wife died, then the husband married a second wife and he died, the second wife and her heirs come before the first wife's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married the first wife and she died, then married a second and he died, the second wife and her heirs come before the heirs of the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second case to the ruling in step 11. Now the first wife is no longer alive when the husband dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 both wives outlived the husband, so the first wife, or her heirs, came first. Here the first wife died before him, and the order flips. The second wife, and her heirs, come before the heirs of the first wife.
steps.whatToRemember: First wife alive: she comes first. First wife died before the husband: the second wife and her heirs come first.

phrases.english: If he married the first wife and she died,
and he married a second wife and then he died —
the second wife and her heirs come before
the heirs of the first wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשָׂא אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וָמֵתָה, נָשָׂא שְׁנִיָּה וּמֵת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the same משנה begun in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first wife died before the husband, the second wife and her heirs have priority over the first wife's heirs.

steps.title: Reading the word 'precedes' in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה says the first wife 'precedes' the second. It does not say the second wife has no rights at all. So if the second wife seized property first, we would not take it from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה says 'the first precedes the second' and not 'the first has rights and the second has none,' it implies that if the second went first and seized property, we do not take it away from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by pulling a hidden point out of the משנה's exact wording. This sets up the general rule it will try to prove in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'precedes' sounds like the second wife still has a real claim. She just stands second in line. So if she grabbed property first, she would have taken something that is rightfully hers, and we would leave it with her.

keyTerms.meaning: from the fact that it teaches
we do not take it away from her

phrases.english: GEMARA
From the fact that it teaches "The first precedes the second,"
and it does not teach
"The first has rights and the second does not have rights,"
this implies that if the second went first and seized property —
we do not take it away from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: That a second wife who seized property first keeps it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's choice of the word 'precedes' instead of 'only the first has rights.'

steps.title: A proposed general rule about a later creditor
steps.stepSummary: From this inference the גמרא suggests a general rule. A later creditor who collected before an earlier one keeps what he collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a later creditor who went first and collected keeps what he collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the point from step 13 and turns it into a wide rule about all creditors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second wife is like a later creditor, and the first wife is like an earlier creditor. If the second wife keeps what she seized, then any later creditor who collected first should also keep what he got.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
a later creditor
phrases.notes: 'Later' means his loan document is dated after the other creditors' documents.

phrases.english: who went first and collected —
what he collected, he has collected.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בַּעַל חוֹב מְאוּחָר שֶׁקָּדַם וְגָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the inference from step 13 into a general rule about creditors.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a later creditor who collected first keeps what he collected.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'precedes,' as read in step 13.

steps.title: 'Precedes' can mean 'completely comes first'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A later creditor really does not keep what he collected. 'Precedes' means the first wife comes first completely, just like 'a son precedes a daughter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, I can tell you: what he collected, he did not get to keep. What does 'precedes' mean? It means completely, as we learned: a son precedes a daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from steps 13 and 14 by reading the word 'precedes' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In inheritance, 'a son precedes a daughter' means that when there is a son, the daughter gets nothing at all. In the same way, 'the first precedes the second' can mean the second wife has no right here. So the משנה proves nothing about a later creditor who grabbed first.

keyTerms.meaning: actually, I can tell you (the opening of a rejection)
as we learned in a משנה
a son comes before a daughter (in inheritance)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'precedes' does not prove the second wife keeps what she seized. It can mean 'comes first completely,' as in 'a son precedes a daughter.'
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'precedes' as 'both get paid, just in order.' Here the גמרא says it can mean that the one who comes second gets nothing.

phrases.english: Actually, I can tell you:
what he collected — he has not collected,
phrases.notes: He means the later creditor has to give back what he took.

phrases.english: and what does "precedes" mean?
It is teaching "completely,"
as we learned: a son precedes a daughter.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא בתרא about who inherits.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ: מָה שֶּׁגָּבָה לֹא גָּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in steps 13 and 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה for the rule that a later creditor who collected first keeps what he collected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'precedes' means 'both have rights, only in order.' It can also mean 'completely comes first,' as in 'a son precedes a daughter.'

steps.title: Second version: the משנה's silence means we take the property from the second wife
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the גמרא reads the משנה's silence as meaning that if the second wife seized property first, we take it away from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the discussion went like this. The משנה does not say, 'If the second wife went first and seized property, we do not take it from her.' So we can infer that if she went first and seized property, we do take it away from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version (איכא דאמרי) of the earlier inference. This time it learns from what the משנה leaves out that the second wife's seized property is taken back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 13), the word 'precedes' was read to mean the second wife keeps what she grabbed. Here the reading flips. If the משנה meant she keeps it, it should have said so outright. Because it says nothing, she must lose it.

keyTerms.meaning: She seized (took hold of property on her own)
We take it out of her hands

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions! In the first version the inference was that the second wife keeps what she seized. In this version (איכא דאמרי) the inference is the opposite: we take it from her.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
From the fact that it does not teach:
"If the second wife went first and seized property,
we do not take it from her,"
we can infer that if the second wife went first and seized property
we do take it away from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of steps 13–15, reading the משנה the opposite way.
steps.raayaObject: That the second wife's seized property is taken back from her
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's silence: it never says 'we do not take it from her'

steps.title: Proposed rule: a later creditor who collected first loses what he took
steps.stepSummary: From this inference the גמרא suggests a general rule. A later creditor who collected before an earlier one must give back what he collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a later creditor who went first and collected, what he collected is not truly collected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the inference about the second wife into a general rule for all creditors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second wife's כתובה is a later debt than the first wife's. If her seized property is taken back, then any creditor with a later debt who grabbed first should also lose it. This is the reverse of the rule suggested in the first version (step 14).

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this: a proposed proof or conclusion
A later creditor: one whose debt was made after another's

phrases.english: Learn from this:
a later creditor
who went first and collected,
what he collected, he has not collected.
phrases.notes: He means it does not count, so it is taken back from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general creditor rule from the inference in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: A later creditor who collected first loses what he collected
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from the משנה in step 16

steps.title: Rejection: a later creditor keeps what he collected, and the wording comes from the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A later creditor really does keep what he collected. The משנה's wording is explained by its next clause about the second wife and the first wife's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, I will tell you that what he collected, he has collected. But since the משנה taught: 'The second wife and her heirs come before the heirs of the first wife,'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proposed rule. It begins to explain that the משנה's wording comes from its later clause. The explanation finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא holds that a later creditor who collected keeps it. The משנה's later clause is about the first wife's heirs, who collect as an inheritance and not as a debt. There it makes sense to take back what they seized. The גמרא is starting to show that the earlier clause simply used the same kind of wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I will tell you: introduces the rejecting view
Since it taught: the wording follows another clause

phrases.english: Really, I will tell you
what he collected, he has collected,
but since it taught:
"The second wife and her heirs come before
